newsitem.title: JAPAN: DLR STEADY VS YEN IN TOKYO, RECOUPS EARLIER LOSSES.
newsitem.headline: DLR STEADY VS YEN IN TOKYO, RECOUPS EARLIER LOSSES.

text.p: 0002 GMT --*Dollar mostly steady against yen in early going after earlier losses were offset by mark buying against yen in cross trade by Japanese operators.
*But traders keen to sell dollars on rises on perceptions that dollar's topside edging down and due to overnight falls particularly against mark, dealers said.

*Buying by Japanese investors expected to emerge at around 115.20-30 yen and below 115 yen, although their heavy purchases since earlier this week failed to lift dollar much due to active selling by U.S. funds operators, they said.
*"There is a sense that the dollar's ceiling is becoming lower and long positions have been squared," said a dealer at a U.S. bank.
*He said although Japanese life insurers bought dollars at below 115.50 yen overnight after heavy selling by U.S. funds at 115.90 yen, its recovery had been slow.
*Dollar's topside capped at around 115.80 yen after recovering from earlier low of 115.47 yen in early Asian trade.
*Dealer at U.S. bank said dollar may seek its floor against yen and mark in near term. Focus on release of Japan's customs-cleared trade data for July due out on Monday.
*Reuters poll of economists produced average forecast of an 83 percent rise in its trade surplus from a year ago.
*Forecasts ranged from a 60 percent to a 114 percent increase in the surplus, or a surplus of 799 billion yen to 1.07 trillion yen.
*Overnight, dollar was hurt by expectations of higher German interest rates and report suggesting Europe's single currency might be postponed.
*Bundesbank also warned of rising consumer prices and said it would gear monetary policy towards keeping inflation under control.

*A senior dealer at a Japanese bank said that dollar would probably fall as low as 1.8180 marks due to growing expectations for higher German interest rates, although quick credit tightening unlikely.
*Dealers also doubted early German interest rate rise, given its weak economy and ahead of European single currency.

*A trust bank dealer said he would also closely watch the U.S. stock market."If the current corrective phase in the stock market prolongs, investments in dollar assets will not revive and will limit the dollar's rise," he added.
